sara: Heads up — noticed a p99 spike on host streaming paths after yesterday's runtime deploy (r3108). p50 stable but tail jumped ~2x. Starting quick triage, looks parse/tokenization heavy. Anyone already on this?

jin: I pulled a perf sample off a canary. flame shows parse_token dominates, lots of memcpy and grpc_readv on the hot path.

```
# perf top -p <pid>
  parse_token        46.3%
  grpc_readv         18.2%
  kv_cache::lookup   12.1%
  memcpy              9.4%
  other               14.0%
```

oliver: That matches a hypothesis I had — the tokenizer was materializing tiny buffers for each chunk and doing a full copy before parsing. I prototyped using iovec (scatter/gather) and a streaming token iterator to avoid the memcpy.

oliver: Quick numbers from a local canary run (mix of short and long streams):
- baseline (r3108): p50 8ms, p95 18ms, p99 42ms
- iovec-token patch: p50 7ms, p95 12ms, p99 27ms

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for r3109 -> 5% traffic.

maria: Also noticed KV cache hit ratio dipped around the same deploy window. Hits: 94% -> 88% in the raw traces; could amplify tail if parse path changes key form.

jin: Good catch. I instrumented the key normalization path — we were including an ephemeral trace prefix in the cache key for some streaming routes (introduced in r3099). Quick normalization fix (strip trace prefix) bumped hit rate back to ~93%.

jin: With both fixes applied in a combined canary test: p50 7ms, p95 10ms, p99 22ms (end-to-end host-side).

oliver: Opening PR with: iovec tokenization change, token iterator, kv key normalization, and an optional gRPC small-write coalescing flag at the proxy level. Tests included (microbench + e2e perf harness).

jin: I also tweaked batching heuristics: if prefix cache hit > 60% then prefer immediate dispatch (don't wait for N tokens); this avoids tail from cache-heavy short requests. Locally reduced p99 by a further ~2ms for chat-like traffic.

sara: Nice work. Plan: hold canary at 20% for 2 hours with perf dashboards watching p99, kv hit rate, and grpc write latency. If stable, promote to 100% and roll notes. Also record the kernel selection side-effect note: the reduced memcpy lets backend kernel choose lower-latency path for short sequences.

maria: Running long-run telemetry job now, will post aggregated hit rates / percentile charts in ~90m.

oliver: PR link (draft): https://git/repo/pulls/1234 — contains perf artifacts, flamegraphs, and a small patch to enable tcp coalescing at the proxy.

jin: One more: added a short perf harness case that simulates frequent tiny streaming frames (50B-500B). If you run it: `./bench/stream_small.sh --workers 64 --duration 120` — shows the biggest wins.

sara: Thanks — once canary passes, add a short blurb to release notes and update the dashboard widgets. Great catch on the key normalization, and nice low-risk iovec approach. :tada:
